L1.name: Device Hardware
L1.description: Calls about faults or physical conditions in the computer’s core hardware, including power, charging, displays, input devices, cooling, and physical enclosure damage.

L1.name: Software & Data
L1.description: Calls about Windows startup and recovery, software stability and activation, account access, computer setup, data migration, backups, and data recovery.

L1.name: Connectivity & Peripherals
L1.description: Calls about connecting or using networks, ports, docks, printers, cameras, audio devices, and other attached or wireless peripherals.

L1.name: Purchases & Coverage
L1.description: Calls about warranty protection and transactions involving recently purchased or defective computers, including returns, refunds, exchanges, replacements, and coverage changes.

L1.name: Repair Services
L1.description: Calls about initiating, coordinating, tracking, and resolving paid or warranty repair work, including shipping logistics and onsite service.

L1.name: Support Administration
L1.description: Calls about reaching the appropriate support channel and correcting customer or device records needed for support, registration, or repair processing.

L2.name: Power and Charging
L2.description: Calls about powering on, sudden shutdowns, sleep and wake behavior, charging failures, batteries, chargers, charging ports, and power problems after repair.

L2.name: Warranty Coverage
L2.description: Calls about warranty status, dates, terms, geographic scope, accidental-damage coverage, eligibility, purchasing or extending protection, activation, and coverage-related billing or records.

L2.name: Display and Video
L2.description: Calls about internal or external display output, including screen artifacts, blank or black screens, brightness controls, monitor setup, display cables, and video connections.

L2.name: Input Devices
L2.description: Calls about laptop touchpads, keyboards, keyboard backlights, and wireless mouse or keyboard peripherals that are not working, damaged, intermittently failing, or difficult to configure.

L2.name: Windows Startup and Recovery
L2.description: Calls about BIOS and firmware access, missing boot devices, automatic repair or restart loops, BitLocker recovery, and creating or using Windows recovery media.

L2.name: Software and Account Access
L2.description: Calls about productivity software installation or licensing, account verification, forgotten credentials, Windows PIN or biometric sign-in, tablet account locks, and scam or antivirus prompts.

L2.name: Camera and Audio
L2.description: Calls about built-in cameras, microphones, speakers, headphones, and Bluetooth audio devices that are not detected, connected, or producing usable input or output.

L2.name: Repair Logistics
L2.description: Calls about repair fulfillment choices, shipment tracking, shipping boxes and labels, delivery addresses, local repair providers, and logistics after a repair or warranty purchase.

L2.name: Windows Software and Performance
L2.description: Calls about Windows upgrades and activation, recurring crashes or freezes, application instability, and severe general system slowness.

L2.name: Repair Case Management
L2.description: Calls about following up on open support or repair cases, checking case status, coordinating onsite technicians, and escalating unresolved repair or warranty matters.

L2.name: Network Connectivity
L2.description: Calls about joining Wi-Fi, Ethernet, or hotspots, internet access, wireless disconnections and slow speeds, Wi-Fi drivers, and replacement wireless hardware.

L2.name: Returns and Replacements
L2.description: Calls about returning, exchanging, refunding, replacing, or trading in recently purchased or defective computers, including replacement requests after repeated repair failures.

L2.name: Physical Device Damage
L2.description: Calls about physically damaged screens, hinges, casing, or display separation that may require repair or replacement.

L2.name: Setup and Data Migration
L2.description: Calls about setting up or registering a new computer, transferring files or programs, restoring factory settings, backing up personal files, and recovering data from a failed drive.

L2.name: Support Routing
L2.description: Calls about finding the correct support channel, transferring to another department, reaching language-specific support, or confirming support phone numbers and eligibility.

L2.name: Repair Service and Eligibility
L2.description: Calls about starting paid or warranty repair, no-boot repair service, system-board replacement, replacement-board defects, and repair charges or eligibility.

L2.name: Hardware Compatibility and Ports
L2.description: Calls about hardware compatibility, expansion features, storage or memory detection, USB-C or Thunderbolt port failures, and related device capabilities.

L2.name: Docking Stations
L2.description: Calls about dock compatibility, dock operation, dock firmware or cables, and monitors or power dropping out while connected through a dock.

L2.name: Thermal and Fan Issues
L2.description: Calls about loud or abnormal fans, overheating, fan failure, thermal shutdowns, and buzzing or rattling that requires fan repair.

L2.name: Customer and Device Records
L2.description: Calls about correcting customer contact details, device serial numbers, identifiers, registration records, or other information needed for support and repair processing.

L2.name: Printer Support
L2.description: Calls about installing, connecting, configuring, or troubleshooting printers, scanners, print jobs, and printer drivers.

L3.name: Touchpad not working or intermittently failing
L3.description: Customers report touchpads that stop responding, lose the cursor, behave erratically, or disappear from settings. The shared driver is a laptop touchpad functionality failure, with only a few physical-condition or click-related variations.

L3.name: Built-in camera not detected or working
L3.description: Customers report that the laptop’s integrated camera fails, shows a blank or black image, or is unavailable in video applications. This cluster focuses on camera functionality, including detection and intermittent failures, rather than microphone or speaker audio.

L3.name: Productivity suite installation and license activation
L3.description: Customers mainly need help installing, activating, transferring, or regaining access to purchased or included productivity applications, especially Microsoft Office and Microsoft 365. A few requests concern email, antivirus subscriptions, administrator access, or migration, making this cluster broader than the account sign-in cluster.

L3.name: Screen distortion, flickering, or panel damage
L3.description: Customers report colored lines, pixelation, flickering, corrupted images, backlight failures, blackouts, or physical screen damage that may require replacement or warranty service. It is distinct from screens that remain completely blank and from blackouts tied to startup, power, or specific use conditions.

L3.name: BIOS update, settings, or recovery failure
L3.description: Customers need help with BIOS or firmware updates that fail, roll back, or leave the computer in recovery, as well as related BIOS settings, passwords, and boot-mode changes. The cluster covers firmware-level access and update problems rather than Windows application or hardware-peripheral issues.

L3.name: External monitor connection and setup
L3.description: Customers ask how to connect, configure, cable, or use one or more external monitors directly with a computer. This cluster is broader setup and compatibility guidance, rather than problems specific to a docking station.

L3.name: General power-on or startup failure
L3.description: Customers report varied inability to turn on, start, boot, or remain powered on, including issues involving the power button, reset attempts, or initial setup. Unlike the other power clusters, these requests do not consistently mention missing charging lights, sudden onset, or a prior repair.

L3.name: Operating system upgrades and update failures
L3.description: Customers ask whether the computer can receive a major operating system upgrade or need help installing, troubleshooting, or manually applying system updates. The cluster centers on upgrade eligibility and update installation problems, rather than activation or product licensing.

L3.name: Dock compatibility and general function
L3.description: Customers ask about docking station compatibility, detection, replacement, firmware, cables, and general operation, including dock ports and support for multiple displays. This differs from the neighboring cluster focused specifically on monitor and power dropouts while docked.

L3.name: Computer speakers or audio output silent
L3.description: Customers report no sound, missing audio devices, muted or distorted speakers, or unreliable output from built-in and wired external audio equipment. This cluster centers on general audio output rather than Bluetooth pairing or microphone input.

L3.name: Cracked or shattered laptop screen repair
L3.description: Customers seek repair, replacement, quotes, or warranty information for cracked, shattered, or otherwise externally damaged laptop screens. A few requests mention dents or damaged casing, but the primary issue is screen damage rather than hinge failure.

L3.name: Check existing repair case status
L3.description: Customers want updates on repair tickets, orders, parts, approvals, shipping information, quotes, cancellations, or work orders. Unlike cluster 29, these requests primarily ask for the current status or outcome of an existing repair process.

L3.name: Laptop returns, refunds, and exchanges
L3.description: Customers ask about returning recently purchased computers or accessories, obtaining refunds or shipping labels, and exchanging products within the return window. This focuses on standard purchase-return logistics rather than replacement of a defective device through support.

L3.name: Charger or charging port replacement
L3.description: Customers request replacement or purchase of defective, damaged, missing, or incompatible chargers, power cords, and related power supplies, or report damaged or loose charging ports. This cluster focuses on the external power accessory or charging-port hardware rather than the laptop's general power-on behavior.

L3.name: Forgotten Windows PIN or password access
L3.description: Customers cannot access Windows because they forgot, do not know, or changed the sign-in PIN or password, including on newly set up or shared computers. This cluster is broader than the PIN-specific sign-in failures in the neighboring cluster.

L3.name: Account sign-in and verification during setup
L3.description: Customers call because account login, password, or verification steps prevent new-computer setup or access to applications and email. This is distinct from the productivity software cluster because the primary obstacle is account authentication rather than installing or licensing software.

L3.name: Replace laptop instead of warranty repair
L3.description: Customers request a replacement for a defective or nonworking laptop rather than sending it for warranty repair, including after a recent repair. This differs from repeated-failure replacement requests because the main issue is avoiding or bypassing the repair process.

L3.name: Keyboard keys intermittently fail
L3.description: Customers report keyboard keys or sections that work inconsistently, including intermittent typing, beeping, sticking, or repeated characters. This differs from clusters focused on consistently nonworking keys, physical damage, or complete keyboard failure.

L3.name: Built-in microphone not recording properly
L3.description: Customers call about an integrated or headset microphone that is not detected, produces very low or poor-quality audio, or intermittently stops working in meetings and recordings. It is distinct from camera problems and from failures involving audio output through speakers or headphones.

L3.name: No power with no charging indicator
L3.description: Customers report that the laptop will not power on or charge, typically with no charging or status light. This distinguishes the cluster by the absence of power indicators, unlike general startup failures or post-repair failures.

L3.name: Recurring BitLocker recovery prompt or loop
L3.description: Customers report repeated BitLocker recovery screens that block startup, resets, or factory restoration, and may ask how to disable the recurring prompt. This differs from other clusters focused primarily on retrieving a missing key or recovering data.

L3.name: Find the correct technical support channel
L3.description: Customers seek the appropriate support department, phone number, website path, or service channel for varied products and needs. This cluster is broader and more routing-oriented than the warranty-specific clusters.

L3.name: Check standard warranty status and terms
L3.description: Customers ask whether a computer remains under warranty and how particular warranty terms affect repair, performance, opening the device, ownership transfer, or warranty linkage. This is a general status-and-policy cluster rather than one focused on a specific failure or damage event.

L3.name: Follow up on existing support case
L3.description: Customers seek access, status updates, case numbers, or continued assistance for recently opened technical support cases. This cluster centers on ongoing case follow-up rather than escalation or shipment changes.

L3.name: Repair and replacement case logistics
L3.description: Customers call about tracking, turnaround, shipping, depot or in-person repair options, onsite service, replacement shipments, and data handling during repair. This is broader repair and replacement logistics rather than only checking an existing technician case.

L3.name: Missing boot device prevents startup
L3.description: Customers encounter missing or selectable boot-device errors, an absent operating system, or a system that opens BIOS instead of Windows. The defining issue is failure to locate the drive or boot target, rather than a general recovery loop.

L3.name: Warranty upgrade for onsite coverage
L3.description: Customers ask to upgrade or extend warranty coverage to include onsite, premium, or accidental-damage support, often requesting pricing. A few requests concern specific repair or software coverage and the warranty impact of a user-installed SSD, but the main driver is expanded warranty protection.

L3.name: Extend or renew expired warranty coverage
L3.description: Customers ask to lengthen warranty protection, including after expiration, and add future repair, onsite, accidental damage, or software support. This differs from general warranty purchases because the focus is extending or renewing coverage terms.

L3.name: Correct warranty dates and coverage records
L3.description: Customers ask to correct or verify warranty start dates, expiration dates, purchase details, and international coverage records. This differs from the other clusters by focusing primarily on the accuracy and scope of warranty records rather than repair handling or extension pricing.

L3.name: Black screen with system unresponsive
L3.description: Customers report a completely black or blank display associated with freezing, failed startup, inability to log in, or other unresponsive behavior. This differs from the other display cluster, where the computer continues running despite the black internal screen.

L3.name: Black internal screen while system runs
L3.description: Customers report that the laptop powers on and continues running, with keyboard lights, fans, time display, or an external monitor working while the built-in screen remains black or extremely dim. The defining feature is an active system behind the failed internal display.

L3.name: Check hardware compatibility and related features
L3.description: Customers ask whether hardware, ports, storage slots, expansion cards, drivers, and accessories are compatible, with a few related questions about SD card slots and cloud-storage warnings. The cluster is broader and more exploratory than Cluster 92's reports of hardware not being detected or operating incorrectly.

L3.name: Windows PIN or biometric sign-in failure
L3.description: Customers are unable to sign in because the Windows PIN is rejected, unavailable, or stuck, often alongside failed facial recognition or fingerprint authentication. It focuses on PIN and biometric sign-in malfunction rather than primarily forgetting an unknown password or credential.

L3.name: Keyboard keys consistently not responding
L3.description: Customers report specific keyboard keys or groups of keys that no longer register, including laptop, desktop, external, and function keys. Unlike the intermittent-failure cluster, these requests describe persistent key-level nonresponse.

L3.name: Laptop battery drains too quickly
L3.description: Customers report short battery life, rapid or overnight discharge, reduced capacity, and requests for battery replacement or improved runtime. One request concerns changing the charging limit rather than rapid drain, but battery charging behavior is the shared theme.

L3.name: Battery will not charge or hold charge
L3.description: Customers report the battery staying at zero, failing to charge, or dying immediately when unplugged. This cluster focuses on the battery itself, including a request to identify a replacement battery.

L3.name: Automatic repair loop prevents startup
L3.description: Customers report repeated automatic or startup repair screens, recovery errors, or corrupted system files that prevent booting and login. This differs from the missing-boot-device cluster because the system enters recovery or repair instead of primarily reporting no boot device.

L3.name: Intermittent freezing and application crashes
L3.description: Customers call about computers freezing, becoming unresponsive, or occasionally crashing and closing applications during normal use. Unlike the nearby crash clusters, these reports primarily concern hangs and instability during active use rather than boot or recovery loops.

L3.name: Repeated crashes, blue screens, or restarts
L3.description: Customers report frequent system crashes, blue-screen errors, sudden shutdowns, or restarts, generally during startup or normal Windows operation. This is distinct from recovery-loop cases because the main concern is recurring crashes or stop errors rather than failure to complete automatic repair.

L3.name: Connect laptop to networks and hotspots
L3.description: Customers need help connecting the laptop to available Wi-Fi networks, routers, Ethernet, school networks, or phone hotspots. This cluster is distinguished by the focus on joining specific networks or personal hotspots.

L3.name: Wi-Fi adapter, network, or driver failure
L3.description: Customers report missing Wi-Fi options, unavailable networks, adapter problems, driver reinstallation failures, DHCP issues, or recurring wireless failures. These requests emphasize an underlying Wi-Fi component or configuration fault rather than simply connecting to a network.

L3.name: Check current warranty activation status
L3.description: Customers ask whether coverage is active, expired, newly purchased, or when an extended warranty will take effect. This cluster centers on verifying coverage status and dates rather than purchasing or activating the plan.

L3.name: Correct device serial number or ID
L3.description: Customers need serial numbers, device IDs, motherboard identifiers, or related registration details corrected, recognized, or programmed for support and repair processing. Most requests concern identifier mismatches or rejected identifiers, with a few involving tools or IDs for specific device components or services.

L3.name: Repair shipment address and box issues
L3.description: Customers call about receiving, resending, redirecting, or canceling repair shipping boxes and replacement-part shipments. These requests focus on repair shipment logistics and delivery destinations rather than changing the repair service type.

L3.name: Wireless mouse and keyboard setup or failure
L3.description: Customers mainly need help using wireless mouse and keyboard peripherals, including missing receivers, setup, and unresponsive input. A few requests instead concern touchpad repair follow-up or purchasing a compatible pen, making this cluster broader than the primary wireless-peripheral issue.

L3.name: Broken laptop hinges needing repair
L3.description: Customers report cracked, broken, loose, or separating hinges and request repair or depot service. Unlike the adjacent cluster, the hinge is the main reported failure without a broader combination of detached screen and casing damage.

L3.name: Computer completely dead, no power
L3.description: Customers report no power, lights, indicators, or response when attempting to turn on the computer or monitor. These cases are distinct from crash and restart issues because the system does not power on at all.

L3.name: Laptop powers on but screen stays blank
L3.description: Customers report a laptop that appears to power on but shows no image or illumination at all, including after a screen replacement or hard reset. The defining issue is persistent blank display output rather than intermittent blackouts or visible screen artifacts.

L3.name: Intermittent Wi-Fi disconnections and slow speeds
L3.description: Customers report recurring Wi-Fi drops, inability to reconnect, weak or unreliable connections, latency, and very slow speeds across one or more networks. The cluster is distinguished by ongoing connection instability rather than post-reinstallation driver setup or hardware replacement.

L3.name: Recover BitLocker key after hardware change
L3.description: Customers mainly need to locate or use a BitLocker recovery key to unlock the computer, especially after a system board or motherboard replacement. A few requests involve keyboard or USB input problems during recovery, with one unrelated activation-key outlier.

L3.name: Transfer to correct support department
L3.description: Customers request transfers to Premier, technical, gaming, specialized, human resources, or language-specific support teams, including after a prior transfer was disconnected. The defining issue is being routed from the current interaction to another department.

L3.name: Post-expiration warranty coverage questions
L3.description: Customers ask whether repairs remain covered after expiration, what basic coverage includes, and whether coverage or eligibility is current. This cluster centers on interpreting coverage around expiration, rather than correcting records or arranging a repair.

L3.name: System board replacement and repair support
L3.description: Customers seek replacement or warranty assistance for failed internal components, especially motherboards, and help after board repair. This differs from general out-of-warranty repair and no-boot service through its focus on component or system-board replacement.

L3.name: Defective device replacement or trade-in
L3.description: Customers seek to return faulty devices for a replacement or refund, compare replacement prices, or obtain trade-in credit. It differs from the broader purchase-return cluster by emphasizing defective-device resolution and replacement value, with one unrelated software request.

L3.name: Change or cancel repair service type
L3.description: Customers want to switch between onsite, depot, or local authorized service, or cancel an existing repair request. The defining issue is changing the repair fulfillment method or service case status.

L3.name: Track repair shipment deliveries
L3.description: Customers ask where repair boxes, labels, recovery media, return materials, replacement devices, or related communications are in the delivery process. This cluster focuses on shipment tracking and delivery status rather than preparing or resending materials.

L3.name: Obtain and prepare repair shipping materials
L3.description: Customers need a repair box, label, shipping address, or replacement shipping materials, or ask how to package the computer and what accessories to include. This differs from cluster 23 by focusing on obtaining and preparing materials rather than tracking delivery.

L3.name: Physically damaged keyboard needs replacement
L3.description: Customers primarily seek repair or replacement for a broken or damaged keyboard, often requesting onsite service or a replacement keyboard assembly. One request concerns restoring keyboard-language switching, but the dominant driver is physical repair or replacement.

L3.name: Complete keyboard failure and replacement options
L3.description: Customers report a keyboard that has broadly or completely stopped working, sometimes after a repair, update, or screen replacement, and may need a replacement or compatible alternative. This is broader than individual unresponsive keys and is distinct from requests centered on physical damage.

L3.name: Keyboard diagnosis, power, and connection issues
L3.description: Customers report varied keyboard hardware and connectivity problems, including no typing despite lights, charging or power failures, RGB behavior, recovery-environment issues, and suspected heat damage. The cluster combines several diagnostic scenarios rather than one narrowly defined keyboard failure.

L3.name: Laptop USB-C port hardware failures
L3.description: Customers report USB-C, Thunderbolt, or related laptop ports failing to charge, carry display output, or recognize connected devices. These are laptop port or controller problems, rather than failures of the docking station itself.

L3.name: AC adapter or charging cable not working
L3.description: Customers report that the charger, adapter, or charging cable does not supply power, sometimes only working when positioned a certain way. This differs from battery-focused issues because the suspected failure is in the external charging equipment.

L3.name: Boot-time recovery and restart loops
L3.description: Customers report systems repeatedly shutting down, restarting, or getting stuck at the manufacturer logo or automatic repair process. The cluster is distinguished by failed startup and recovery sequences rather than isolated crashes during normal use.

L3.name: Replacement or upgrade Wi-Fi hardware
L3.description: Customers want to purchase, replace, upgrade, or return physical Wi-Fi or network-card hardware, including compatibility questions. This concerns the wireless component itself rather than installing drivers or troubleshooting connection drops.

L3.name: Printer installation and printing problems
L3.description: Most customers need help installing printers or drivers, connecting network printers, resolving print errors, or fixing scanning and printed-output issues. PDF annotation and Quicken display problems are unrelated software outliers.

L3.name: Back up or restore personal files
L3.description: Customers ask how to preserve, recover, or restore personal files before repairs, resets, or operating system changes, or report that files are missing. This differs from Cluster 105, which focuses on data recovery from a failed hard drive, and Cluster 6, which focuses on recovery media.

L3.name: Scam security pop-ups and antivirus removal
L3.description: Customers call about alarming fake security warnings, persistent scam pop-ups, or antivirus software that is blocking the computer or repeatedly prompting. This differs from the other clusters because the focus is malware-like alerts and unwanted security software rather than account, operating system, or productivity software access.

L3.name: Set up and register a new computer
L3.description: Customers seek help getting a newly purchased computer ready for personal use, including initial setup and product registration. This differs from factory-reset requests because the goal is configuring a new device rather than restoring it.

L3.name: Replace laptop after repeated repair failures
L3.description: Customers seek replacement or refund after multiple unsuccessful repairs, recurring shutdowns, crashes, or unresolved hardware problems. The defining factor is repeated repair failure rather than simply preferring replacement for a new or unrepaired device.

L3.name: Escalate unresolved repair or warranty case
L3.description: Customers primarily want a supervisor or senior manager to address unresolved repair or warranty concerns. A few requests involve contacting a prior representative, obtaining a customer number, or purchasing software support.

L3.name: Keyboard backlight failure and settings
L3.description: Customers report keyboard lighting that does not work, is uneven, or stops intermittently, and ask how to adjust brightness or color. All requests concern keyboard backlight operation or configuration rather than general keyboard key failures.

L3.name: Dock monitor and power dropouts
L3.description: Customers report a dock intermittently or consistently failing to detect monitors, provide adequate laptop power, or maintain charging and display connections. One request mentions phantom inputs, but most concern display and power behavior through a dock.

L3.name: Bluetooth headphones or speakers lack audio
L3.description: Customers report Bluetooth audio devices that fail to connect, disconnect, power on, or produce sound. Most requests concern wireless headphones or speakers, distinguishing this cluster from general speaker output and microphone issues.

L3.name: Hinge-related screen detachment damage
L3.description: Customers report hinge damage accompanied by a detached, cracked, or nonresponsive screen, or separation between the display and the laptop base. This cluster is distinct from hinge-only repairs because the hinge failure has caused broader screen or casing separation.

L3.name: Severe laptop slowness and lag
L3.description: Customers call about very slow booting, browsing, application use, downloads, or overall system performance, sometimes worsening after extended use or software changes. Most requests concern broad laptop slowness, with a few focused specifically on internet download speed.

L3.name: Loud fan and general overheating
L3.description: Customers call about excessively loud fan operation, device heat, and sometimes reduced performance during normal use. Unlike the other fan clusters, these requests generally seek diagnosis of noisy or hot operation without a clearly reported fan failure or mechanical buzzing.

L3.name: Power failure after prior repair
L3.description: Customers say the laptop still will not power on or work after a depot, warranty, or other prior repair. The defining feature is recurrence or persistence of the problem following repair service.

L3.name: Recover or replace failed hard drive
L3.description: Customers report a crashed or inaccessible hard drive and ask about recovering files, replacing the drive, or obtaining related recovery information. This cluster is centered on hard-drive failure and non-booting systems rather than routine backup or creating recovery media.

L3.name: Storage drive and memory not detected
L3.description: Customers report startup or usability problems caused by undetected storage drives or incorrect or unavailable memory. This differs from Cluster 17 because these calls concern hardware detection and memory behavior rather than upgrade compatibility or feature guidance.

L3.name: Operating system activation, edition, and S mode
L3.description: Customers need help with operating system activation, missing or incorrect edition licenses, identifying the original license, or leaving restricted S mode. This differs from the update cluster because the issue is licensing or software restrictions after or independent of updating.

L3.name: Activate or manage warranty renewal
L3.description: Customers report problems activating, reinstating, or registering purchased or renewed warranty coverage, along with a renewal payment page or auto-renewal request. This differs from status inquiries because the customer needs an activation or account-management action.

L3.name: Warranty extension pricing and terms
L3.description: Customers ask about the cost, payment terms, validity period, reinstatement fees, and recognition of warranty extensions or upgrades. The defining issue is purchasing or reinstating additional coverage.

L3.name: Warranty repair eligibility and charges
L3.description: Customers seek to confirm that a repair is covered, whether diagnostic or labor charges apply, what information is needed, or how to start a warranty repair. This cluster focuses on initiating and validating a repair under existing coverage.

L3.name: Check coverage for accidental damage repairs
L3.description: Customers ask whether repairs are covered after drops, liquid damage, severe physical damage, hacking, crashes, or other specific incidents. The defining feature is coverage for damage or an incident rather than routine warranty status.

L3.name: Replace recently purchased laptop
L3.description: Customers ask to replace a newly purchased or malfunctioning laptop, obtain a newer replacement, or address a physical defect present since purchase. These requests focus on replacement of a recent purchase, including purchases from a retailer, rather than failed warranty repairs.

L3.name: Find authorized local repair provider
L3.description: Customers seek a nearby authorized repair center or want to arrange covered service through a local provider. Some also ask about repair estimates or reimbursement for local repairs, distinguishing this cluster from requests to replace the computer or correct its identifiers.

L3.name: Update customer account contact information
L3.description: Customers primarily request changes to account details such as address, phone number, or email. A few requests concern email administration, server alerts, or obtaining a repair shipping label, making this cluster less focused.

L3.name: Follow up on existing support case
L3.description: Customers seek assistance or callbacks for an already opened support, repair, or order case. This is broader than the technician-specific coordination in cluster 89 and less focused on status tracking than cluster 26.

L3.name: Existing repair status and technician scheduling
L3.description: Customers primarily want updates on an open repair or replacement case, including technician visit timing and delivery status. This cluster is more narrowly focused on monitoring and scheduling already-created repair cases.

L3.name: Device will not power on or charge
L3.description: Customers report Chromebooks, laptops, or a tablet that will not turn on, show charging, or respond after charging and reset attempts. The cluster is focused on complete power or charging failure rather than battery runtime.

L3.name: Sudden shutdown and power failure
L3.description: Customers report that the laptop suddenly stopped working, shut down, or became unable to power on, including after an update or before reaching network access. The cluster is distinguished by the sudden onset or shutdown context rather than a persistent no-indicator condition.

L3.name: Charging failure despite replacement chargers
L3.description: Customers report that the computer does not recognize chargers, show a charging indicator, charge the battery, or power on even after trying multiple or replacement chargers. It is broader than the other charging clusters and includes a tablet charging issue.

L3.name: Sleep, wake, or unexpected power cycling
L3.description: Customers report problems entering sleep, waking from sleep, or unexpectedly waking and powering on. This differs from general crashes because the issue is tied specifically to sleep and lid-close behavior.

L3.name: Black screen triggered by login, movement, or video
L3.description: Customers report the display going black after Windows appears, immediately after login, when the lid or display is moved, or while video applications are open. These are usage- or transition-triggered blackouts rather than a continuously blank screen or primarily power-related failure.

L3.name: Wi-Fi driver installation after Windows reinstall
L3.description: Customers need to restore Wi-Fi or install the wireless driver after reinstalling or clean-installing Windows, often without an active internet connection. These requests focus on driver availability and setup rather than defective hardware or intermittent connectivity.

L3.name: Create or obtain Windows recovery media
L3.description: Customers need a Windows recovery USB or factory recovery image, or encounter errors while creating or using recovery media to reinstall the operating system. Unlike Cluster 105, the main issue is the recovery media or reinstallation process, not a failed hard drive.

L3.name: Screen brightness controls not working
L3.description: Customers report that the display stays dim, changes brightness incorrectly, or ignores brightness-key and monitor controls. This cluster focuses specifically on malfunctioning brightness adjustment rather than general display problems.

L3.name: Language-specific support connection requests
L3.description: Customers ask to connect with support or sales representatives speaking French, Spanish, or English, with one broader software-support connection request. This concerns reaching an appropriate language or support line, rather than transferring an active call between departments.

L3.name: Support phone number or eligibility information
L3.description: Customers seek the correct support phone number, phone menu, or confirmation that they qualify for a support service, with one request to reconnect to a prior representative. This cluster is primarily about finding or validating the right access route rather than requesting an active department transfer.

L3.name: Purchase additional warranty coverage
L3.description: Customers want to buy an extended or upgraded warranty for one or more devices, often while limited coverage remains. This cluster focuses on purchasing added protection rather than checking status or resolving activation problems.

L3.name: Warranty duration, region, and hardware coverage
L3.description: Customers ask about warranty length, coverage by purchase region, and whether hardware problems such as power or charging failures are covered. It is distinguished by questions about geographic scope, duration, and basic hardware-failure eligibility.

L3.name: Out-of-warranty repair options
L3.description: Customers ask about paid repair availability, costs, or warranty-status corrections for computers outside coverage. This cluster is defined by repair eligibility after warranty expiration rather than a specific hardware symptom.

L3.name: No-boot or no-power repair service
L3.description: Customers need repair for laptops or desktops that will not boot, start, or turn on, usually under warranty. It is distinguished from other repair clusters by the prominent no-start symptom.

L3.name: Coordinate onsite technician repair
L3.description: Customers call about missed technician callbacks, rescheduling appointments, restarting technician work, or understanding closure of an onsite repair case. The defining feature is direct coordination with a field technician or onsite work order.

L3.name: Fan failure causing overheating and shutdown
L3.description: Customers report extreme CPU overheating, fan failure alerts or nonfunctioning fans, severe slowdown, and unexpected shutdowns. This cluster centers on critical thermal failure rather than ordinary fan noise.

L3.name: Fan buzzing or rattling needing repair
L3.description: Customers report unusual buzzing or rattling from the fan and often ask for expedited repair or warranty coverage. A few requests involve fan errors, overheating, crashes, or failure to boot, making this somewhat broader than the primary noise complaint.

L3.name: Desktop powers on with no display
L3.description: Customers report a desktop or all-in-one that powers on but produces no monitor image or video signal, sometimes with beeps or a black screen. This cluster focuses on complete loss of video output rather than display distortion or intermittent blackouts.

L3.name: Intermittent black screen tied to power or startup
L3.description: Customers report black screens that recur depending on charger connection, unplugging, startup errors, or similar power-related conditions. This differs from blackouts triggered by login, opening or rotating the display, or video applications.

L3.name: Internet connectivity stopped or unavailable
L3.description: Customers report that the laptop cannot access the internet through Wi-Fi or Ethernet, including cases where Wi-Fi appears to work. This is a broad internet-access problem rather than a request focused on connecting to a particular network or fixing the wireless adapter.

L3.name: Tablet locked by forgotten PIN or account
L3.description: Customers cannot access a tablet because of a forgotten PIN, a previous owner's account, or a lock triggered after resetting the device. The stolen-device tracking request is an outlier, but most requests concern tablet access and account locks.

L3.name: Recover or reinstall Windows without BitLocker key
L3.description: Customers are trying to regain access, recover files, reset the laptop, or reinstall Windows when the BitLocker recovery key is unavailable. This is distinct from recurring BitLocker prompts and from key retrieval tied to hardware replacement.

L3.name: Check accidental damage warranty coverage
L3.description: Customers ask whether accidental physical damage, battery issues, or device replacement are covered, or whether an accidental coverage purchase is active. The defining topic is the scope and status of accidental damage protection.

L3.name: Repair logistics after warranty purchase
L3.description: Customers ask about repair return shipping, diagnostic fee treatment, or canceling a repair after obtaining or using warranty coverage. It differs by focusing on the practical handling of a repair after a warranty purchase or repair request, rather than initial coverage verification.

L3.name: Verify warranty coverage and recurring charges
L3.description: Customers want to validate warranty status, reconcile conflicting coverage information, or understand a recurring service payment. It differs from general warranty-status questions through its emphasis on discrepancies and billing-related coverage.

L3.name: External display cable or port failure
L3.description: Customers report missing video or a failed cable or display port when connecting a monitor or television. It is distinct from the broader monitor setup cluster because these requests focus on a nonworking connection, with one unrelated screenshot request as an outlier.

L3.name: Replacement motherboard installation defects
L3.description: Customers report problems with replacement system boards, such as failed memory slots, undetected graphics hardware, short risers, or damage causing no power. This cluster concerns replacement-board fit, compatibility, or component functionality rather than general motherboard failure.

L3.name: Transfer files and programs to new computer
L3.description: Customers want to move files, applications, or software from an old computer to a new one. This differs from general new-computer setup because the main need is migration of existing data and programs.

L3.name: Restore computer to factory settings
L3.description: Customers want to return a computer or tablet to its factory state, including after setup or login problems. This differs from new-computer setup because it involves resetting an existing configuration rather than establishing one.
